questions.q: An operator notices a mixing step ran five minutes longer than the batch record says. What is this called?
questions.why: A deviation is any departure from an approved procedure or instruction, recorded and investigated.

questions.q: A lab result falls outside the approved specification limits. What is it called?
options: A warning letter from the regulator
A change request in the eQMS
questions.why: OOS means a test result outside approved limits, which must be investigated.

questions.q: Which US rule covers electronic records and electronic signatures?
questions.why: 21 CFR Part 11 sets the rules for electronic records and signatures in FDA-regulated work.

questions.q: At the end of an inspection, an FDA investigator hands over a list of observations. What is that document?
questions.why: A Form 483 lists observations at the end of an inspection. A warning letter is a later, formal and public notice.

questions.q: Which phase of qualification checks that equipment works across its operating range?
questions.why: OQ is operational qualification. IQ checks installation and PQ checks performance in real use.

questions.q: A record shows a value but not who entered it. Which ALCOA+ principle is broken?
questions.why: Attributable means every entry can be traced to the person or system that made it.
